solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One shouting below is in the right

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other, so the word for below goes into the middle of the other pair

parts.note: below means under

explanation.surface: Someone yelling from downstairs claims to be in the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One shouting' could be a cheering fan, but THUNDERER is also an old nickname for The Times newspaper itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A thunderer is a person who roars or bellows with great force of voice.

clue.text: It's Susan in the paper!

parts.note: 'tis is the old poetic contraction of it is
Sue is the short form of the name Susan

explanation.surface: An excited cry on spotting a friend named in the newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Tissue is a thin, soft kind of paper, as in tissue paper used for wrapping.

clue.text: Put exercise into German and turn over

indicators.note: into tells us the exercise letters are placed inside the German word

parts.note: und is the German word for and
PE stands for physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: An instruction to slot some exercise into German and then flip something over.
explanation.definitionFit: To upend something is to tip it upside down, a synonym for turning over.

clue.text: Detective raised Lancastrian symbol almost in confusion

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means the letters are written upwards, so read backwards
almost means the last letter is left off

parts.note: the red rose is the emblem of the House of Lancaster and of Lancashire

explanation.surface: A detective holds up a Lancashire rose in some bewildered scene.
explanation.walkthrough: The red rose is Lancashire's emblem; 'almost' drops its final E, and 'raised' reads the rest upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Disorder is a state of muddle or chaos, a synonym for confusion.

clue.text: Easily defeat, by circling quickly?

definitions.meaning: to outclass an opponent with ease is an idiom for this
the phrase read literally describes running in loops around someone fast

explanation.definitionFit: To run rings round someone is an idiom meaning to outperform them effortlessly.

clue.text: Talk wildly, not at first serious

indicators.note: not at first means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: grave means serious

explanation.surface: Someone babbles wildly, not being serious to begin with.
explanation.definitionFit: To rave is to speak incoherently or with frenzy, a direct synonym for ranting.

clue.text: Drop long tale that needs shortening

indicators.note: shortening means the last letter is cut off the word

parts.note: a saga is a long story

explanation.surface: Cut a rambling story that has become too long.
explanation.definitionFit: To sag is to sink or droop downwards, a synonym of drop as a verb.

clue.text: In second place, encourage to spend heavily

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names
urge means encourage

explanation.surface: Someone who came second is urged to go on a spending spree.
explanation.definitionFit: To splurge is to spend extravagantly on a treat, a synonym for spending lavishly.

clue.text: Farmhouse and good grazing land

parts.note: a range is open land where livestock graze

explanation.surface: An estate agent's line: farmhouse with good pasture.
explanation.definitionFit: A grange is a country house with farm buildings attached, so a farmhouse.

clue.text: Looks for some Indians to pick up

indicators.note: picking up here means catching what is heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: Sikhs are followers of Sikhism, many of them from the Punjab in India

explanation.surface: Someone searches for a group of Indians to collect in a car.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeks is a synonym of searches for, in the same third-person form as looks for.

clue.text: Book is new to American city

parts.note: novel means new or original
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A book arrives fresh in an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: A novella is a short novel, so a kind of book.

clue.text: Be the cause of stress, forgetting name

indicators.note: forgetting the name means leaving out its letter

parts.note: to underline something is to stress it

explanation.surface: Stress is to blame for forgetting someone's name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be the cause of' looks like a link phrase, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To underlie something is to form its basis or root, so to be its cause.

clue.text: Daughter has tatty garment: a man wears it?

parts.note: a rag is a worn-out piece of clothing

explanation.surface: A daughter owns a shabby piece of clothing that a man might wear.
explanation.definitionFit: Drag is women's clothing worn by a man as a performance, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Tradesman's entrance finally crossed by trailer manoeuvring

definitions.note: read as Tradesman is, the 's linking definition to wordplay

indicators.note: crossed by means the letters of the other piece run across this one, around it
the trailer is being manoeuvred into a new position, so its letters are rearranged
finally picks the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A tradesman's back entrance is blocked by a reversing trailer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tradesman's entrance' is a stock phrase, but the definition stops at 'Tradesman's'; E, the last of 'entrance', goes inside a rearranged TRAILER.
explanation.definitionFit: A retailer is a shopkeeper who sells goods, a kind of tradesman.

clue.text: Pestered, look embarrassed about association

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: to be red in the face is to look embarrassed
a league is an association of clubs or people

explanation.surface: Someone harassed looks sheepish when asked about a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'look embarrassed' is a two-word phrase giving a two-word piece: to be red in the face.
explanation.definitionFit: Beleaguered means beset by troubles or harassment, close to pestered.

clue.text: Make clear it's no longer simple?

parts.note: ex means former, something that no longer is
plain means simple

explanation.surface: A wry question: does clarifying something stop it being simple?
explanation.definitionFit: To explain is to make something understandable, a synonym of clarify.

clue.text: Such a meal might make friends?

parts.note: pals are friends; the answer read as instructions writes the word for them upwards, as in this down entry

explanation.surface: A lavish dinner might help you win friends.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer, read as wordplay, means 'slap written upwards', which in a down entry reads PALS, the friends.
explanation.definitionFit: A slap-up meal is a British idiom for a lavish, generous feast.

clue.text: Best carbon goes into the processing of steel

indicators.note: goes into means one piece is placed inside the other
processing works the steel into a new form, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: Top-quality carbon is used in steelmaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Select describes something chosen as the finest, a synonym of best as an adjective.

clue.text: Liberal program for Northerner

parts.note: an app is a computer program

explanation.surface: A Liberal software project aimed at someone from the north.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lapp is one of the Sami people of far northern Scandinavia, so a northerner.

clue.text: Blame rep for messing up introduction

indicators.note: messing up the words jumbles their letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A salesman is blamed for botching a presentation's opening.
explanation.definitionFit: A preamble is an opening statement or preface, a synonym for introduction.

clue.text: Set time to be introduced to composer

indicators.note: being introduced to something here means put inside it

parts.note: J S Bach was a German composer

explanation.surface: A time is fixed for someone to meet a composer.
explanation.definitionFit: A batch is a group of things produced or dealt with together, a synonym for set.

clue.text: Second-class egg-whisk, I may say

indicators.note: the setter is saying it, so the word is taken by how it sounds in speech

parts.note: a beater is a kitchen tool for whisking eggs

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that their egg-whisk is a second-rate gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: BEATER sounds like BETA in a non-rhotic British accent.
explanation.definitionFit: Beta is the second Greek letter, used as a grade for second-rate work.

clue.text: Even out gold on dish

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another comes after it, so the gold is placed second

parts.note: a plate is a dish
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Smooth gold leaf evenly over a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: To plateau is to level off after rising, a synonym of even out.

clue.text: Flexible and somewhat slithery

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of the word is used, a run of its letters

explanation.surface: Something bendy and a little snake-like.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithe means supple and agile, a synonym of flexible.

clue.text: What one may be putting towards cask

definitions.text: What one may be putting towards
definitions.meaning: in golf, the flagstick in the hole is what a player putts at
a small barrel holding four and a half gallons

explanation.definitionFit: The pin is the golfer's flagstick, and a pin is also a small beer barrel.

clue.text: Trees popular in military town

parts.note: alders are trees of the birch family
hot means popular or in demand

explanation.surface: Trees are much in favour in a garrison town.
explanation.walkthrough: ALDERSHOT is a Hampshire town known as the home of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: Aldershot is the traditional home of the British Army, the archetypal garrison town.
